newsitem.title: SPAIN: Repsol surges again on unsatisfied demand.
newsitem.headline: Repsol surges again on unsatisfied demand.

text.p: Shares in Spain's Repsol outperformed stock indices on Wednesday, buoyed by strong demand after a successful privatisation, dealers said.
At 1315 GMT Repsol was up 70 pesetas (48 cents), 1.16 percent, to 6,110 pesetas while the Ibex-35 blue chip index was up 0.25 percent to 5,853.04.
"Basically the placement went very well and there's obviously a lot of unsatisfied demand out there," said a dealer at a Spanish bank.
"Saving surprises, I think we could see Repsol back up at 6,300 pesetas as soon as next week," he added.
His year end target price for Repsol was at around 7,000 pesetas.
The Spanish state sold its last 10.0 percent stake in Repsol in a public share offering which ended on Friday.
The retail tranche, for which 60 percent of the shares were allocated, was oversubscribed around 45 times while the institutional tranche was overbid more than nine times.
An analyst at BZW in London said the stock was benefiting from analyst presentations ahead of the public share offering.

"I think the massive round of presentations is behind the buying interest... A long term price target could well be at around 7,000 pesetas if the company achieves its targets in terms of profit in the next five year. But I have to say they're ambitious," he said.
Dealers said that final foreign clients were buying, as well as traders. Volume at mid-afternoon was over two million shares.
Ahead of the privatisation, Repsol chairman Alfonso Cortina said the firm was aiming to double net and operating earnings by the year 2001.
